decisions.rationale: "retinoblastoma" names a specific disease, but in "retinoblastoma phenotype" it modifies the noun "phenotype" rather than standing alone as a disease mention, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 (Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: In "retinoblastoma-predisposition gene", "retinoblastoma" modifies the noun "gene" and does not itself denote a disease, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 (Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: "tumors" refers to the retinoblastoma tumors that spontaneously regressed in these families, linked to one specific disease. The guidelines explicitly retain "tumor" and "cancer" as disease mentions rather than excluding them as general terms.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); What NOT to Annotate §4 ("cancer" and "tumor" are retained)

decisions.rationale: "tumorigenesis" denotes a biological process (the development of tumors), not a disease mention, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §5 (References to biological processes, e.g. tumorigenesis)
